Sod Installation in Guelph

A finished lawn in a day, built on the prep work that decides whether new sod actually roots.

Get a Free Quote Call or Text

★★★★★  75+ five-star Google reviews

When a lawn is too far gone for overseeding — mostly bare, mostly weeds, torn up after construction or a dug-up trench — new sod is the fastest way back to a usable lawn. We remove the old turf, prepare and level the soil, then lay fresh sod tight with staggered seams and roll it so the roots meet the soil.

Most of the work in a good sod job happens before the first roll goes down. Guelph’s heavy clay packs hard and sheds water, so the ground is loosened and graded to drain away from the house first. Sod laid on compacted, uneven clay roots shallowly and struggles every July.

The service

From tired turf to a new lawn

  • Old grass, weeds and debris stripped and removed
  • Soil loosened, levelled and graded to drain away from the house
  • Fresh sod laid tight, with staggered seams and no gaps
  • Rolled for firm root-to-soil contact, then watered in
  • A clear aftercare plan: watering, first mow, first feeding

Sod makes sense after renovations and new builds, where a lawn has thinned beyond repair, or where you need a usable yard quickly rather than waiting a season for seed to fill in.

Local know-how

Sod or overseeding? How we decide

Sod isn’t always the right answer, and we’ll say so. If your lawn still has a reasonable base of grass, core aeration and overseeding costs far less and thickens it within a season. Sod earns its price when most of the area is bare soil or weeds, when the grade needs fixing, or when you need the yard usable now.

Read more

Timing in Guelph. The best windows are spring, once the ground has thawed and dried out (usually May into June), and late summer into early fall, when nights cool down and rain is more reliable. Sod can go down in midsummer, but it needs much more water to survive the heat — and outdoor watering in Guelph follows the City’s Outside Water Use program, so check the current level first (our bylaw explainer).

Never over old grass. Laying sod on top of an existing lawn leaves a spongy layer of dead turf between the new roots and the soil. The old lawn comes off first, every time.

Pricing

What affects the price of sodding

Every sod job is quoted on your actual property, after we’ve seen it. The main factors:

  • Area in square feet
  • Removing and disposing of the old turf
  • How much levelling or grading the soil needs
  • Access — open front yard versus a backyard behind a narrow gate
  • Slopes and awkward shapes that need more cutting

You’ll get a firm price before anything is booked. No contracts, no deposit games.

Aftercare

The first four weeks

  • Weeks 1–2: keep the soil under the sod moist, not just the blades. Lift a corner: the soil should be damp.
  • Weeks 2–3: taper to deeper, less frequent watering as roots take hold. Keep foot traffic light.
  • First mow: once the sod resists a gentle tug, usually two to three weeks in. We cut at 3 inches, and can add it to your weekly mowing.
  • First feeding: after it has rooted, a balanced fertilizer helps it thicken before its first winter.
Common questions

Sodding questions

When is the best time to lay sod in Guelph?

Spring once the ground has dried out, usually May into June, and late summer into early fall. Midsummer installs can work, but they need far more water to survive the heat.

Should I sod or overseed?

If your lawn still has a reasonable base of grass, aeration and overseeding is cheaper and very effective. Sod makes sense when most of the area is bare or weeds, the grade needs fixing, or you need a usable lawn quickly.

How much do I water new sod?

Enough to keep the soil underneath moist, not just the grass — usually daily for the first week or two, then tapering to deeper, less frequent watering as it roots. Check the City of Guelph’s current outside water use level before setting timers.

When can I walk on new sod?

Light foot traffic after about two to three weeks, once it has rooted and resists a gentle tug. Keep heavy use — play, parties, dogs running laps — off it for the first month.

Can you lay sod over my existing lawn?

No. Sod laid over old grass and weeds sits on a spongy dead layer and roots poorly. The old turf is always removed first.

How much does sodding cost?

It depends on the area, turf removal, how much levelling the soil needs and access to the yard. We quote each property after seeing it, with a firm price before anything is booked.
